Subject: VPC deployment pricing — platform fee carveout & exit credits?

Hi Markus,

Thanks for taking the call yesterday. We loved the demo — performance looked solid for our use cases. Before we move to procurement, two quick commercial asks from our finance & cloud teams:

1) Platform fee carveout: Can Redwood carve out the platform fee for the first 12 months (or amortize it across the committed term) for a VPC/on‑prem deployment? It’s a sticking point for our capital team.

2) Exit/rollback credit: Because we’ll be doing a staged migration across three sites, can you provide an exit/rollback credit (for unused months of platform fee) if we decommission a site within year one?

We also need to understand support tier options and typical SLA ramp for private deployments (oncall expectations, response windows for SEV1/SEV2). I attached our internal procurement checklist — happy to add any other docs you need.

If you can share a short commercial sketch by Monday that we can take internally, that will keep momentum.

Best,
Alex
Director, Cloud Operations
Cerulean Health

Subject: Commercial sketch: VPC deployment — amortization & credits

Alex — attaching a short commercial sketch and the pricing workbook for your finance team. Key points below so you can share quickly:

- Proposed structure (high level)
  • Licensed nodes: upfront perpetual license per node, with an optional 36‑month amortization schedule that spreads the licensing cost across the committed term for accounting friendliness.
  • Platform fee: default is annual platform fee equivalent to 12% of first‑year licensed node spend. Options: full upfront, 12‑month carveout (credit applied as invoice credit spread over first 12 months), or amortized across committed term.
  • Migration credit (one‑time): we propose a migration credit equal to 10% of first‑year committed spend applied if Cerulean signs a minimum 24‑month commitment. Credit is forfeited if termination occurs before 12 months.
  • Exit/rollback credit: capped at 25% of remaining platform fee for any decommissioned site within year one; credit applied as refund or invoice credit depending on billing preferences.

- Support tiers (EU private deployment)
  • Standard: Mon–Fri 09:00–18:00 CET, 4‑hour SEV1 response, business hours SRE support, ticketed escalation path. (Included)
  • Premier: 24x7 oncall with 1‑hour SEV1 response, weekly operational reviews, 8 oncall incidents included per year. (+15% of first‑year spend)
  • Enterprise SRE Retainer: Named SRE time blocks (monthly), dedicated runbook creation, and guaranteed on‑site/remote runbook runoffs for major cutovers. (POA)

- Other mechanics
  • DocuSign flow for commercial redlines — we can split platform fee across invoices if that helps procurement.
  • Pricing workbook attached with line‑items + example amortization schedules.

Attached: pricing_workbook_vpc.xlsx; draft SOW stub embedded as Cerulean_SOW_v2.pdf.

Next steps: we can 1) send a redlineable term sheet for procurement, or 2) if you prefer, Marissa and I can host a 30‑minute call with finance tomorrow to walk through the workbook. Which do you prefer?

Thanks — Marissa
Senior Director, Commercials
Redwood Inference

Couple of operational clarifications we should include in the customer sketch before we hand to procurement:

1) SLA & oncall specifics for Exit Credit cases: if Cerulean decommissions a site within year one and claims exit credit, we need a 30‑day notice and an agreed deprovisioning playbook. Our credit processing requires confirmation that KV caches and logs have been securely wiped or migrated.

2) Data residency & retention addendum: for EU sites please confirm whether Cerulean expects 3rd‑party backup retention outside of the EU — this affects our optional enterprise SRE retainer pricing.

3) DocuSign & signature flow: Procurement sometimes routes to their corporate DocuSign and wants the platform fee split into 2 invoices (pilot vs production). We can support that; will add conditional language.

I’ve drafted two short paragraphs to drop into the SOW (see attached SOW stub). Recommend we also add a one‑line KPI rollback condition tied to migration milestones (so credits don’t kick in unless migration progresses to stage N).

— Irene
Director, Deploy & Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Subject: Final commercial counter / next steps (Cerulean Health)

Alex — thanks for the patience while we aligned internally. Below is a succinct customer‑facing counter that preserves what you asked for while keeping our billing and risk boundaries clear. This is ready to be turned into a redlineable term sheet; I’ve included the DocuSign link in case procurement wants to move quickly.

Commercial counter (summary):
• Minimum commitment: 24 months for VPC license across all three EU sites; example line‑items in attached workbook.
• Platform fee: 12% of year‑one licensed node spend. Options: (A) Carveout credit applied as a one‑time invoice credit across first 12 months (we apply a negative invoice for month 1–12), or (B) amortize platform fee across the 24‑month commitment at Cerulean’s election.
• Migration credit: 10% of year‑one committed spend if Cerulean signs the 24‑month commitment. Credit is applied 30 days after sign and pro rata applies if sites are added later. Credit is forfeited if contract terminates before month 12.
• Exit/rollback credit: For any site decommissioned within the first 12 months, credit limited to 25% of remaining platform fee for that site, subject to 30‑day decomm notice and completion of deprovisioning checklist (secure KV wipe & log export confirmation).
• Support: Standard tier included. Premier (24x7 oncall / 1‑hour SEV1 response) available at +15% of first‑year spend. Enterprise SRE Retainer priced POA; will provide an estimate on request.

Attachments: Cerulean_SOW_v2.pdf (SOW stub with milestone‑tied credit language); pricing_workbook_vpc.xlsx (line item and amortization examples).

Next steps: 1) Marissa or I can post the redlineable term sheet to DocuSign (link below) — we recommend procurement review and return with any must‑have redlines. 2) If helpful, schedule a 30‑minute walkthrough with finance + our commercial ops to confirm amortization examples.

DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.com/recent/cerulean-vpc-ds-9f7a

If this aligns, procurement can route the redline back to me and I’ll shepherd it through for exec approval.

Best,
Markus
